newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian Authority says 1996 bank deposits up.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian Authority says 1996 bank deposits up.

text.p: The Palestinian Monetary Authority (PMA) said on Tuesday that bank deposits in the West Bank and Gaza rose by 47 percent in 1996 to $1.722 billion from $1.174 billion in 1995 as the financial sector continued to expand.

In a statement summing up 1996 economic activity in the Palestinian self-rule areas, the PMA, which acts as a central bank but does not issue currency, said assets of the 17 banks operating in the West Bank and Gaza Strip stood at $2.213 billion, up by $574 million from 1995.

Palestinian economists say the increase in deposits despite declining economic conditions may be because more Palestinians have been putting into the banks savings they kept at home or abroad before the 1993 Israeli-PLO self-rule deal.
Commercial banks had made loans of $431 million in 1996, an increase of 68 percent from $174 million over 1995.
The statement said the 17 banks operated 71 branches in the West Bank and Gaza in 1996. In 1995, there were only 13 banks with 57 branches.
Only five of the 17 banks were owned by Palestinians, the statement said. Eight were owned by Jordanians, two by Egyptians, one by Australians and one Israelis.
It said the Monetary Authority has given preliminary approval to eight more domestic banks to be established in the self-rule areas.
